boundary_decision.rationale: Both providers independently reached entry_kind=aggregate for vr.wm-blt-006, and both independently rejected the two collapse candidates: Facility into Site (rejected because ISO 41011 and IfcSite/IfcFacility keep land locus distinct from operating asset collection) and Facility into Building (rejected because IFC 4.3 subtyping is recorded as an alignment conflict, not adopted as the registry relation). The registry CONTAINS edge to WM-BLT-001 is retained as operational aggregation; Site containment is retained as conditional because IFC permits a facility aggregated directly to a project with no site. No split, reclassification or merge is warranted: the boundary between the Facility aggregate and the Facility Management management system (ISO 41001) is stated identically by both providers.

decisions.rationale: Claude states twelve in-scope and twelve out-of-scope items each keyed to a named sibling model, gives eight source-referenced boundary notes, and carries the governance spine the merged model needs (bitemporal versioning, retention and disposition, disclosure control, crosswalk lossiness). Grok's bundle set is wider but its boundaries repeat inside findings rather than being declared once; size was not the deciding factor.

Independent agreement between providers, and both reached it by rejecting the same two collapse candidates (into Site and into Building) with the same primary evidence, which is stronger than mere agreement on a label.

decisions.concept: Facility CONTAINS Building versus IFC 4.3 IfcBuilding-as-subtype
decisions.disposition: Retained as recorded alignment conflict; registry CONTAINS relation kept
decisions.rationale: Both providers independently declined IFC conformance and recorded the inversion. Base additionally prescribes that a single-building facility maps directly to IfcBuilding in the crosswalk rather than to IfcFacility plus a redundant child, which resolves the practical case without changing the boundary.

decisions.disposition: Conditional edge to WM-BLT-008, not mandatory
decisions.rationale: IFC permits a facility aggregated directly to a project with no site, and both providers reached this conclusion separately. The composition link must therefore be marked not-required rather than assumed.

Base only carried this reasoning in adversarial checks; a registered agent needs a first-class test that rejects a single asset, an unbuilt asset, a kind-of-location classifier, or a room, and admits civil and mobile facilities.

decisions.concept: Certificate of occupancy as authorization gate
decisions.disposition: Accepted from grok, bounded to reference plus scope and validity
decisions.rationale: Distinct from occupancy classification, which the base already holds. The instrument's issuance workflow and conditions text stay in the Authorization sibling model per the base out-of-scope list, so the addition does not breach the declared boundary.

Base tracks open nonconformities but not the legal weight of a reported determination or its refresh lag. Misreporting alleged as adjudicated is a concrete downstream harm and the ECHO data dictionary supports the distinction directly.

Base risk coverage is exposure and continuity plus protective security; fire risk, sprinkler and exit provisions and emergency preparedness were genuinely absent. Accepted with the source's own caveat that detailed life-safety design belongs to Building and Space models.

decisions.disposition: Accepted from grok, service-life portion suppressed
decisions.rationale: POE is defined in ISO 41011 and placed on the ISO 19650-3 operational timeline and is missing from the base. Service life remains mastered by the base condition-and-service-life finding to avoid two masters for the same measure.

decisions.concept: Grok identifier, naming, address and coordinate findings
decisions.rationale: Base already covers master key and external registry precedence, non-reuse, merge and split, alias validity, address roles and jurisdiction, CRS, vertical datum, accuracy, level of detail and relative-versus-absolute placement. Adding these would create parallel structure without new decision surface.

decisions.concept: Grok identity-matching-and-data-quality (no silent merge without steward review)
decisions.disposition: Rejected as a finding; retained as a required answer under the base deduplication question
decisions.rationale: Base already asks what deduplication and match-confidence rule applies and what confidence accompanies matched values. The steward-adjudication control is the answer to those questions, not a separate structure, and duplicating it would split match governance across two layers.

Base operator-and-service-accountability already carries delegated service scope, governing agreement and what the demand organisation retains, and both providers put SLA commercial terms and the FM management system out of scope. Only mobilization state was novel, which is insufficient for a finding.

decisions.disposition: Deferred to the crosswalk matrix, not adopted as structure
decisions.rationale: FHIR Location spans beds, freezers, vehicles and buildings, so adopting it as the facility aggregate would over-cover spaces and kinds; grok itself records this as a conflict. It may be added as a versioned alignment row under the base crosswalk finding once a healthcare profile is validated.

decisions.disposition: Not adopted as bundles; accepted content routed into existing base layers
decisions.rationale: Base already places ownership, custody and operating accountability under authority-tenure-and-compliance and security posture under the same bundle. Creating parallel bundles would fragment authority semantics; the two accepted safety and authorization findings fit existing layers cleanly.

deferred_research: Whether one operational facility may span multiple sites, and by what method area, population and reporting are apportioned when a facility straddles parcels, municipalities, tribal land or utility service territories. Claude allows multi-site with apportionment but states no consulted source prescribes a method; grok records the question as unresolved. Neither position is evidenced, so it must be recorded as an open Dimension decision.

Accessibility designation at facility aggregate level (ISO 21542, ADA and national equivalents). Grok carries only the IFC HandicapAccessible flag and lists ISO 21542/ADA as an omission; claude does not address accessibility at all. Needs a primary source before any finding is created.

Ongoing statutory inspection regimes referenced but not sourced: NFPA 101, 25 and 72, ASME A17.1 and non-US equivalents. Required to give the accepted fire-life-safety finding a defensible inspection cadence rather than a static assertion.

Facility registers outside the US EPA FRS (European PRTR, national real-property inventories and cadastres) to test whether the identifier resolution, programme-interest and regulatory-standing structures survive substitution of the US instruments they were derived from.

Sustainability and green-building certification at facility rather than building level (LEED, BREEAM, EPBD energy performance certificates). Claude rejected it as attractive but insufficiently grounded; grok lists ENERGY STAR as unfetched. Decide only after a facility-level primary source is obtained.

Person-level occupancy, access credentials and workplace monitoring. Claude marks this an explicit coverage gap and holds only aggregate counts; verify whether even aggregate occupancy retention and publication are lawful in strict data-protection jurisdictions before the model is adopted there.

Insurance, valuation and loss-history context, and digital-twin runtime telemetry with control-point naming (Brick, Project Haystack). Both are acknowledged parts of the facility decision surface but neither provider found primary support for a defensible structure.
publication_holds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete: the same EPA Facility Site Identification Data Standard PDF is dated 2014-10-01 Version 2 by claude (SRC-004) and 2006-01-06 Version 2.0 by grok (SRC-003), and the two providers assign it different authority tiers. Re-fetch and pin one date, version and tier before any citation is published.

Pin a single IFC documentation reference: claude cites the ifc43-docs build 4.3.2.20260821 (IFC4X3_ADD2) while grok cites standards.buildingsmart.org IFC 4.3.2.0 mapped to ISO 16739-1:2024. Both URLs must be re-resolved live and one canonical citation chosen for IfcFacility, IfcFacilityPart and IfcSite.

All ISO sources on both sides (41011, 6707-4, 19650-3, 55001, 81346-12, 15686-1) were taken from catalogue or Online Browsing Platform records, not normative clause text. Hold any clause-level or conformance wording; publish alignment language only, and state the non-reading explicitly in the draft.

Claude records that the FY2026 FRPP Data Dictionary and the EPA FIDS PDF could not be machine-parsed, so element names, formats and code values are unverified. Publish these as existence-and-authority citations only; block implementation-level field naming until re-parsed.

Multi-profile domain validation is not complete. The merged evidence is dominated by US federal instruments (FRS, FRPP, NARA GRS 5.4, ISC, IBC, ENERGY STAR, ECHO) plus EU INSPIRE and one healthcare alignment. Validate against at least one non-US built-asset profile and one non-building civil or infrastructure profile before presenting the model as domain-general.

The five accepted grok findings each rest on a narrower evidence base than the base findings around them (IFC property sets for life safety, a single ECHO dictionary for compliance status, one IBC section for occupancy authorization). Mark them as provisionally sourced in the draft and re-verify before they carry any normative weight.
